$comment: Environment identity — the one place a deployed environment's provider IDs are named: its Supabase project, its Render API service, and the Vercel team and projects both environments deploy to. These are NOT secrets: the Supabase project refs already appear in docs/ops/db-rollback-playbook.md, docs/internal/environment/CLOUD_SANDBOX.md and .claude/skills/live-verification/SKILL.md, a ref alone grants nothing without SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, and the Render and Vercel ids grant nothing without RENDER_API_KEY or VERCEL_API_KEY. What IS a secret is the token, and that still comes from Infisical or the GitHub environment. Read this file through scripts/ci/lib/environments.mjs rather than parsing it inline; a workflow reads the provider ids through scripts/ci/provider-ids.mjs, and no workflow names one as a literal (#2806; a test greps for them). `infisicalEnvSlug` values are Infisical SLUGS, not display names — production is `prod`, not `production`; scripts/check-env-slugs.mjs scans this file for exactly that trap. Optional per-environment flag: `allowEmptyMigrationHistory` (default false) tells check-migration-order.mjs that an empty applied-migration list is legitimate rather than a wrong ref — set it only for a genuinely new project, since both projects here permanently hold 00000000000000_initial_schema.
